- [FACT] The appellant’s case involves contractual obligations regarding waterproofing.
- [FACT] The specific contractual terms mentioned are: “waterproofing membrane to sill to be provided by builder” and “responsible for waterproofing of our windows only. If structure is not waterproofed correctly, warranties are voided.”
- [FACT] The appellant claims they are not responsible for the installation of flashing around the windows.
- [FACT] The respondents argue that the terms of the contract were superseded by the Deed.
- [FACT] Clause 14 of the Deed states it constitutes the entire agreement and supersedes any prior understanding or agreement.
- [FACT] Clause 14.1 states it constitutes the entire agreement between the parties as to its subject matter.
- [FACT] Clause 14.2 states it supersedes any prior condition, warranty, indemnity, or representation.
- [FACT] The appellant refers to clause 7 of the Deed, which they argue preserves the terms of the original contract.
- [FACT] The Tribunal addressed the appellant’s submissions regarding waterproofing obligations.
- [FACT] The respondents claim the windows failed due to the builder's failure to install window flashings correctly.
- [FACT] The Tribunal accepted the expert evidence of Mr. Brennan over Mr. Sim regarding window installation.
- [FACT] Mr. Brennan's report dated 17 May 2020 states the responsibility of the window supplier to flash the building element.
- [FACT] Mr. Sim's opinion was that flashing was unnecessary and that the windows were manufactured from commercial grade sections.
- [FACT] The Schlegel Test Report was issued by Schlegel Pty Ltd, an NATA accredited laboratory, certifying a sample window's performance.
- [FACT] Mr. Brennan stated that testing in a “Schlegel portable test rig” did not extend to flashing.
- [FACT] The Tribunal concluded that Mr. Brennan's evidence should be preferred to Mr. Sim's.
- [FACT] The Tribunal determined that the windows leaked due to the absence of small joint sealant.
- [FACT] The Tribunal concluded that the windows were defective and required replacement.
- [FACT] The Tribunal found that the absence of flashing did not alter the conclusion that the windows were defective.
- [FACT] The Tribunal rejected ground 1, stating it involved neither an error of law nor an unfair conclusion.
- [FACT] The Tribunal's conclusion was independent of whether clause 14 of the Deed excluded reference to the original contract.
